payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to reduce electrolyte crossover. An independent Halvorsen-Pike Laboratories audit retracted the earlier 12,000-cycle claim, attributing it to an un-normalized depth of discharge, and established the corrected cycle life at 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold. The battery’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, while its projected stack-level cost is $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its operating-temperature floor is 4 °C, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
